title: WiFi Connect Sequence
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A p5.js step-through sequence diagram of the Chapter 11 Pico W WiFi connect code. Students step through WLAN(STA_IF), active(True), connect(), authentication, DHCP, the isconnected() polling loop, and ifconfig(), and compare success, wrong password, network out of range, and slow router scenarios against an adjustable timeout.

educational.topic: Connecting a microcontroller to WiFi with a timeout
learningObjectives: Put the WiFi connection calls in the correct order
Explain why connect() is followed by a loop that polls isconnected()
Explain what the robot does when the password is wrong, the network is out of range, or the timeout runs out
Choose a timeout that works for a slow router and explain the trade-off
prerequisites: WLAN object and isconnected() from Chapter 11

controls.label: Next Step
controls.purpose: Run the next call (disabled while the loop is waiting)

controls.label: Use secrets.py
controls.purpose: Show the password imported from secrets.py or typed into main.py

simulation.modelType: Step-through sequence diagram with a timed polling loop
equations: loop ends when isconnected() is True or ticks_diff(ticks_ms(), start) > timeout x 1000
assumptions: The loop polls isconnected() every 0.1 s
A normal router connects about 3 s after connect()
The waiting clock runs at 2x real time to save class time
limitations: Does not model WiFi channel, signal strength, or reconnects after a drop
Status code values follow the Raspberry Pi Pico W port

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked example with step-through and failure scenarios
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Next Step / Auto Play sequence diagram with scenario dropdown and timeout slider
keyQuestions: Is the robot connected when connect() returns?
Why do a wrong password and a missing network print the same message?
What timeout would you choose, and what does a longer timeout cost?
What would be exposed if the password were typed into main.py?
commonMisconceptions: connect() waits until the robot is connected
A failed connection always means the password is wrong
A longer timeout has no downside
assessmentOpportunities: Ordering the seven calls before and after the sim
Failure-analysis table with status codes and console output
Exit ticket listing three causes of a failed connection
